html:
The Hopi are a Pueblo people of northeast Arizona, living in villages on three mesas above the Painted Desert. The map shows a much larger area in 1500, a rough label for the farming peoples of the Arizona desert.

The Hopi grow maize, beans and squash in the dry sand with no irrigation, using flood runoff and deep-planted seed. Old Oraibi, built before 1150, is one of the oldest continuously lived-in towns in the United States. Their religion is built around the kachinas, spirit beings who come to the villages in masked dances and bring rain. Their ancestors are the Ancestral Puebloans.

Spanish missions reached the mesas in 1629. In the Pueblo Revolt of 1680 the Hopi killed their priests, and unlike the Rio Grande pueblos they never came back under Spanish rule. Their land is now surrounded by the Navajo Nation. See also Hopitutskwa.
